subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Jill Martin <jill.martin@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & recommended next steps

Hi Sam / Jill 

Thanks again for taking the time today 


Enjoyed the walkthrough of Acme's customer support use case and the traffic/latency constraints you mentioned. As promised, here's a concise recap and a recommended shortlist of models to evaluate against your prompt set. I've attached a one-page shortlist and the benchmark CSV with the numbers from our internal run.

Quick recap:
- Primary requirement: 100-200 ms 95th-percentile latency for single-turn customer replies (short prompts) with high accuracy on entity extraction and concise tone.
- Secondary: multilingual support (EN/ES), inference cost sensitivity - target is < $0.004 per 1k tokens for the baseline production profile.
- Risk: quality regressions when we quantize aggressively; want regression monitoring if we move to int8/4-bit.

Recommended shortlist (high-level):
1) redwood-alpha-7b-quant (int8) - Best cost/latency tradeoff for short responses; slightly lower on complex multi-step extraction.
2) open-llama-13b (fp16) - Stronger extraction/QA quality; higher cost and latency but more robust on edge cases.
3) redwood-chat-3b (optimized) - Lowest latency and cost; good for templated replies and reranking, less ideal for long multi-turn reasoning.

Next steps I suggest:
- Your team: share the most critical prompt templates (we flagged 12 during the call) and 50 representative transcripts for evaluation.
- Our side: run focused evals on those prompts (latency/cost + quality metrics) and return detailed tradeoff matrices and prompts that cause quality deltas. Target to deliver by EOD Thu (2026-07-02).
- Optional: schedule a short follow-up (~30m) to review results and pick a pilot model for a 2-week production trial.

Attachments: redwood-model-shortlist.pdf (one-page), acme-benchmark-results.csv (raw run).

Thanks 

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-model-shortlist.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist & recommended next steps

Sam - great questions, thanks. Short answers up front, then details and links below.

1) redwood-alpha-7b-quant entity extraction regressions:
- Observed a ~3-5% drop in F1 on our internal entity extraction eval when moving from fp16 to int8 for the short prompts set; the drop is concentrated on prompts with unusual punctuation and nested entities. For templated support replies it was negligible.
- Trigger patterns: long context with many parentheses, system messages that inject lists, and multi-lingual code-switching. We'll surface the exact failing prompts in the report.

2) open-llama-13b latency context:
- The numbers in the attached CSV were run on a dedicated-gpu profile (n1-standard equivalent on our Dedicated cluster) to show conservative latency. Shared hosted can be ~10-20% faster on short queues but is less stable under sustained load. We'll mark both numbers in the benchmark.

What I'm sending you today (links + artifacts):
- Benchmark CSV (attached): per-prompt latency (p50/p95), cost-per-1k tokens estimate, and quality metrics (F1/EM/ROUGE where applicable).
- Prompt set: https://docs.redwood.ai/prompt-sets/acme-customer-service-v1 - includes the 12 canonical prompts and scoring rubric.
- Shortlist PDF: a quick rationale per-model (attached).

Rationale (brief):
- redwood-alpha-7b-quant (int8) - pick if latency/cost is the primary driver and the prompts are mostly templated. Recommended safety net: enable prefix caching + an A/B run on 5% of traffic in fp16 to detect any regression.
- open-llama-13b (fp16) - pick if extraction accuracy on edge cases matters more than cost. Recs: use per-route fallback to redwood-alpha-7b-quant for the 90% templated traffic to lower avg cost.
- redwood-chat-3b (optimized) - pick for low-latency canned replies and reranking; not recommended as single model for entity-heavy tasks.

Monitoring & regression plan suggestions:
- Baseline evals: run the 50 transcripts through candidate models and compute per-prompt deltas.
- Continuous quality checks: set up a production eval job that samples 1% of traffic for annotation; alert when F1 drops >3% vs baseline.
- Quantization guardrail: hold back aggressive quantization on routes flagged for entity extraction until we have regression monitoring in place.

I'll run the focused evals and aim to share results EOD Thu. Rafael (cc'd) will chime in with the security/compliance checklist you requested.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Sam / Jill -

Quick note from the security/compliance side - thanks for raising the audit questions on the call. Expect a short checklist and a sample SOC2 evidence bundle by EOD Fri. For the model shortlist: if you plan to run the pilot in your VPC (private deployment) we can provide an HSM/KMS integration guide and the audit log export (daily) so you can ingest into your SIEM.

A few operational notes relevant to model selection: 
- Dedicated vs Hosted: dedicated pools give more consistent p95 latency and easier replay for reproducing a quality regression. Hosted is faster to start and cheaper for low sustained volume.
- Quantization & rollback: we'll include an automated canary rollback policy tied to the evaluation metric you pick (F1 on entity extraction).

I'll attach the compliance checklist now. Let me know if you want us to include sample IaC for the dedicated deployment.

Rafael Mendes
